posts.title: China opposes curbs on hybrid exports to EU, citing WTO rules
posts.summary:
China's commerce ministry rejected voluntary export restrictions on hybrids, saying any solution between China and the EU must comply with WTO rules.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: China's commerce ministry has formally rejected EU requests for voluntary export restrictions on hybrid vehicles, citing violations of WTO rules and market competition principles.
The EU is considering additional tariffs on Chinese hybrids following a surge in imports from 3,800 units in October 2024 to 50,000 in July 2026.
This trade tension marks a new escalation in EU-China automotive relations, as the bloc seeks to prevent domestic deindustrialization following earlier tariffs on battery electric vehicles.

posts.title: Sunwoda joins China's flash charging race with battery system promising 10%-97% in 9 minutes
posts.summary:
Sunwoda said its new system can charge from 10% to 70% in just 5 minutes at room temperature.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Sunwoda has unveiled a 15C smart flash charging battery system capable of charging from 10% to 97% in 9 minutes at room temperature.
The system integrates AI-driven cloud monitoring and fault detection, claiming a 99.77% accuracy rate in predicting potential battery issues.
Sunwoda plans to build an ecosystem of 10,000 megawatt charging stations by the end of 2027 to support its high-rate charging technology.

posts.title: The specter of AI-enabled bioweapons is a wake-up call for biotech
posts.summary: In recent weeks, leaders of some of the biggest AI companies have warned that the very tech they are developing is dangerous. Last weekend, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei argued that AI carries serious risk and that progress should be slowed. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman responded on X: “I agree with Dario that we need to pace the…
bullets: High-level executives at Anthropic and OpenAI have publicly acknowledged the need to pace frontier AI development, citing concerns that the technology could pose catastrophic risks within the next decade.

A 2022 study revealed that an AI model designed for drug discovery could generate 40,000 potential chemical warfare agents in six hours, highlighting the dual-use nature of generative AI in biotechnology.

The ease of access to advanced scientific knowledge via LLMs has created a 'wake-up call' for the biomedical ethics community, as traditional safeguards are struggling to keep pace with the rapid evolution of AI capabilities.

posts.title: Chip Industry Week In Review
posts.summary:
Major memory deal; AI Infra Summit news; U.S. chip capacity plans; 2nm & below advances; Huawei's chip offensive; RoT solution for data centers and AI SoCs; Chinese equipment makers gain share; India's chip build-out; McKinsey's tech trends; major funding rounds; Europe's AI infrastructure gaps.
The post Chip Industry Week In Review appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Infineon is divesting its NOR flash and F-RAM businesses to Winbond for $1.12 billion, a strategic move to focus resources on its core semiconductor segments by 2027.
Huawei is countering U.S. export restrictions by launching an 11-chip AI portfolio and utilizing system-level scaling to improve performance for its upcoming Ascend 960 processors.

The cost of designing a leading-edge 2nm chip has surged to $725 million, creating a significant barrier to entry that threatens to consolidate advanced chip development among only the largest global players.

Applied Materials is committing $5 billion through 2035 to expand its semiconductor research and supply-chain infrastructure in India, signaling a major shift in global manufacturing and R&D footprints.
SK hynix is exploring potential U.S. manufacturing partnerships with Intel, which could involve leasing fab space or forming joint ventures to bolster domestic memory production capacity.

posts.title: 2026.38: Doomforce
posts.summary: The best Stratechery content from the week of September 14, 2026, including the view from anywhere but San Francisco, the limited potential for a pacing deal, and the Salesforce zag.
bullets: Salesforce is pivoting its AI strategy by integrating Anthropic and OpenAI chatbots as the primary user interface, marking a significant shift from its previous focus on proprietary AgentForce tools.

This strategic reversal suggests that enterprise software incumbents are increasingly prioritizing the adoption of third-party frontier models over building walled-garden AI ecosystems to maintain relevance.
While Salesforce aims to monetize this integration by charging a premium, the move risks accelerating the erosion of the traditional SaaS beachhead by commoditizing the underlying software interface.

The Chinese Communist Party remains confident in its ability to manage AI risks, drawing on historical successes in technology control, though rising social media discontent may indicate shifting dynamics in how the state manages public malaise.
